Sundhedsplatformen is a shared healthcare information system utilized by various hospital departments in Denmark. Within the context of national clinical quality databases and registries, the system has been identified as a significant source of data limitation. Specifically, departments operating under Sundhedsplatformen demonstrate a notably poor reporting rate for echocardiography procedures to the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] (National Patient Registry) [^src1]. 

This systemic underreporting has direct implications for national quality assurance metrics. Most notably, it compromises the validity of the results for [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], a clinical quality indicator designed to measure the execution of echocardiography in patients newly diagnosed with atrial fibrillation [^src1]. Because the data submitted from Sundhedsplatformen-affiliated departments is incomplete, it creates an artificially low representation of actual clinical practice, complicating broader RKKP efforts to evaluate and improve cardiovascular care standards across the country [^src1].
